messages:
oncall-bot: SEV alert — streaming service p95/p99 spike detected in eu-west2 (approx 2024-11-03T14:22Z). Alert details: p95=480ms (norm 80ms), p99=2.1s (norm 210ms), streaming reconnect rate x5. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/incoming/alerts/2065001234

oncall-bot: Paging oncall (Liz) and netops (John N)

Liz: I'm on it. I'm seeing tail stalls in the console, opening triage. Starting traceroutes and looking at NAT/ENI stats. John — can you confirm if this is networking?

John N: Yep — initial telemetry shows large increase in TCP retransmits and TLS handshake durations between eu-west2b -> eu-west2c. NAT ephemeral port usage very high on eu-west2b gateway. Suspect ephemeral port exhaustion combined with cross-AZ hairpinning causing SYN retransmits and connection resets.

Maya R: Traces line up with John. Lots of streams stuck in TLS handshake state. p99 cluster around 1800ms-2300ms. Timestamps where spike started ~14:18Z. Also DNS latencies for internal names (cross-AZ) are elevated which is increasing connection setup time.

Liz: Customer impact? Ron, are you seeing anything on CS?

Ron C: CS reports 3 customers with degraded real-time streaming and reconnect loops since ~14:20Z. They see partial payloads and timeouts. I'll send a status note once we have mitigations.

John N: Quick checks from nat-gw-eu-west2b: 
```
# show nat and conntrack
ephemeral_util=96.8%
conntrack_count=185000 (limit 200k)
established_sockets=24k
```
Packet captures show retransmit bursts and duplicated SYNs: 
```
14:19:39.801 IP 10.0.11.45.51234 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [S], seq 0
14:19:40.004 IP 10.0.11.45.51234 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [S] (retransmit)
14:19:40.800 IP 34.56.78.90.443 > 10.0.11.45.51234: Flags [R]
```
That R resets a lot of flows.

Maya R: Also seeing a bump in DNS latency for cross-zone resolvers; that pushed some client libs to retry faster and increased transient socket churn.

Liz: Proposed mitigations (live):
1) Enable prefer-local routing for streaming-eu-west2 route group to force same-AZ ingress/egress where possible.
2) Provision an extra NAT gateway in eu-west2b with expanded SNAT port range and bump conntrack limit.
3) Temporarily throttle per-connection concurrency on streaming frontends to reduce tail load.
4) Notify affected customers with ETA ~20m.

John N: Provisioning extra NAT (nat-extra-eu-west2b) with wider port pool now. Running command: 
```
routerctl create-nat --zone eu-west2b --snat-range 20000-65535 --conntrack-max 400000
```
Attaching ENI and updating route propagation.

DeployBot: Route update: streaming-eu-west2 -> prefer_local=true (propagating)

Maya R: Applying per-conn throttle on frontend pool stream-farm-3: 
```
rbacctl set-rate --pool stream-farm-3 --per-conn 3 --duration 30m
```

John N: New NAT is up and receiving traffic. Ephemeral util fell to ~52% after attachment; conntrack freed space. Seeing TLS handshake tail reduce within 60s.

Maya R: Observed p95 drop from ~480ms -> ~140ms within 90s of route change; p99 trending down from 2.1s -> ~460ms. Streaming reconnects decreasing. Running continuous synthetic streams to validate. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/streams/stream-tail?orgId=1&var-zone=eu-west2b

Ron C: Sending customer update: "We identified a cross-AZ networking egress issue that caused TLS handshake timeouts for some streams. We rolled out routing and NAT mitigations; we expect service quality to improve within ~20 minutes. We'll follow up with a full post-incident update." :white_check_mark:

Liz: Good. Short-term checklist:
- John: keep extra NAT in place for at least 1h and monitor ephemeral/conntrack.
- Maya: continue synthetic tail checks and run regression against baseline prompts.
- Ron: gather affected org IDs and logs, escalate any VIP customers to SA.
- I'll file incident ticket and assign postmortem.

John N: Also enabled temporary kernel tweaks to reduce port reuse delay and increase local port range: 
```
sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range="1024 65535"
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=400000
echo 1 > /proc/sys/net/ipv4/tcp_tw_reuse # temporary
```

Maya R: Launching longer-running validation: tail-distribution job running for next 30m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/alerts/validate-streams-2065001234

Liz: Marking incident as mitigated (impact reduced) but not resolved. Handoff to follow-on oncall for monitoring and postmortem. Handoff note:
- Summary: cross-AZ NAT ephemeral port exhaustion + DNS lat spike -> TLS handshake tail spike -> streaming stalls and reconnects
- Actions taken: prefer-local routing enabled, extra NAT with expanded SNAT range provisioned, conntrack increased, per-connection concurrency limited, kernel port settings adjusted
- Metrics to watch: p95/p99 streaming latency, NAT ephemeral_util, conntrack_count, retransmit rate, internal DNS latency
- Links: alert https://grafana.redwood/incoming/alerts/2065001234, traces https://jaeger.redwood/trace/2065001234
- Current owner: Liz -> follow-up owner: Maya R

Liz: Handoff timestamp 15:07Z. Postmortem required (sev3, network root cause). Ping eng-networking and platform on long-term fixes (autoscale NAT, routing safeguards, ephemeral port guardrails).

DeployBot: Incident channel pinned message updated with incident ticket: https://issues.redwood/INC-206500

Maya R: Taking over monitoring. Will open postmortem draft and include timeline and playbook suggestions.

Ron C: I'll compile customer impact table and send to sales/support.

Liz: thanks team, closing active paging. Continuing to watch for flaps until 16:00Z."
